questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I initially wanted to go to Bologna more than anywhere else because of the culture and tradition and student atmosphere in the city. I ended up in Milan which was my 3rd choice. I accepted it immediately because it was still in Italy which was what my country of preference.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The whole process of going on exchange is very long and tiring. It tones the motivation to go on exchange down a bit. I understand, though, that it is necessary. However when finding proper accommodation is so difficult and expensive as it is in Milan, it gets really annoying being on exchange, out of your comfort zone. Of course I am responsible for not having found proper accommodation before I arrived in Milan but it is extremely difficult! I feel that there should be some extraordinary warning when applying.

The Erasmus Student Network in Milan was great, the university was not. 
- They have no social events for student, or at least exchange students are not made aware. 
- The university is scattered over a vast area of the city. 
- The student information services are very poor. The app is pretty important and it's only in italian. It is really difficult finding your way around the university buildings.
- The structure of classes is in some courses non-existent. It's unclear what the requirements are during the course. In some instances the method of teaching even changed drastically.
- I had a 6ects course with a curriculum of at least 400 pages which is around half of the curriculum of a normal 15ects course at UCPH.
- Italians are terrible at systems and structure. I had an exam where no one in the class was given any information about the exam except for the location. The exam turned out to be pure chaos.
- I was registered for an exam but was removed from the exam again, seemingly without a reason. I didn't even receive any information about the withdrawal of the registration so it was probably just a system failure. That was the last chance to attend that exam and it was not possible to attend exams online.

All in all, I liked the idea of trying new things, being part of another culture but the conditions for a good educational exchange were simply terrible.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of requirements both from UCPH and Statale. I think that is what made it so messy and confusing. A sort of to-do-list would have been nice but it probably still would have been confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction day but that was it. That was really helpful but maybe not quite enough to not feel all on your own.

Additional comments:

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty smooth and easy. The most difficult part was finding universities that are compatible with your studies.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were direct links to the various universities' webpages and course list so that was pretty straightforward. Otherwise there wasn't much help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be really sure that your timetable is a good fit for you and be sure that the courses are actually what you first expect them to be.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see as many cities and places outside Milan as possible. Milan has a lot to offer but you'll find more interesting things that way. In Milan definitely see the San Siro and visit some museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I enjoy the italian culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Simply be quick to talk to people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of structure in Italy is challenging to say the least

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I find their lack of structure annoying but I also like how relaxed they are. Everything is a party in Italy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be sure you pick you picked the right courses.
Be sure you have accommodation when you arrive, and in good area.
Be sure that you're okay with a lack of structure.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything else.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all around the world and practicing a lot of languages.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being a person who needs conformity in a city of chaos.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
